name: lines.saddle.distn
title: Add a Saddlepoint Approximation to a Plot

origin.description: Add a saddlepoint density or distribution function to the current plot.
origin.usage:
lines.saddle.distn(x, dens = TRUE, h = function(u) u, J = function(u) 1,
      npts = 50, lty = 1, ...)

arguments.name: dens
arguments.text: If TRUE, draw the density. If FALSE, draw the distribution function.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: Transformation of the variable. The first argument is the point, and the function must be vectorized.

arguments.name: J
arguments.text: Jacobian of the transformation, used when dens is TRUE. It must have the same arguments as h.

arguments.name: npts
arguments.text: Number of evenly spaced points across the range of the saddlepoint points.
Further arguments passed to h and J.

origin.details: A smoothing spline produces the curve. The density spline is on the log scale and the distribution spline is on the probit scale. The Rd example builds the curve from a bootstrap of 9999 replicates. That bootstrap is omitted here. The coordinates below are the air-conditioning conditional density, which is the curve lines would add.
origin.value: sad.d is returned invisibly. A line is added to the current plot.
origin.example:
air.t0 <- c(mean(aircondit$hours), sqrt(var(aircondit$hours)/12))
air <- saddle.distn(A = cbind(aircondit$hours/12, 1), u = 12, wdist = "p",
                    type = "cond", t0 = air.t0)
tt <- air$points[, 1]
tt1 <- seq(min(tt), max(tt), length.out = 50)
spl <- smooth.spline(tt, log(air$points[, 2]))
exp(predict(spl, tt1)$y)

translation.description: Add a saddlepoint density or distribution function to the current axes and return the coordinates.
translation.usage: lines_saddle_distn(x, dens=True, h=None, J=None, npts=50, lty=1, ax=None, **extra)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict as returned by saddle_distn.

arguments.name: dens
arguments.text: If true, draw the density. If false, draw the distribution function.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: Transformation of the points. None is the identity. Extra keywords are passed through.

arguments.name: J
arguments.text: Jacobian, used for the density. None is 1.

arguments.name: lty
arguments.text: Line type, as an R number or a Matplotlib name.

arguments.name: ax
arguments.text: Axes to draw on. None uses the current axes.

translation.details: The density spline is fit to the log density and the distribution spline to the probit of the cdf. The Rd figure uses boot(R = 9999), which is omitted. This example draws the air-conditioning conditional density. The check times the coordinate arithmetic; the saved figure is the Matplotlib line.
translation.value: A dict with x and y, the coordinates that were drawn.
translation.example:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from boot.data_sets import aircondit
from boot.saddle import lines_saddle_distn, saddle_distn

hours = aircondit()[1][:, 0]
air_t0 = np.array([hours.mean(), np.sqrt(np.var(hours, ddof=1) / 12)])
air = saddle_distn(
    A=np.column_stack([hours / 12, np.ones(len(hours))]),
    u=12,
    wdist="p",
    type="cond",
    t0=air_t0,
)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
drawn = lines_saddle_distn(air, ax=ax)
fig.savefig("packages/boot/docs/output/lines.saddle.distn.svg")
print(drawn["y"])
